claim: A subagent's page is put up at SubagentStart and taken away at SubagentStop by the `state-subagent` hook. Both are detached landings it does not wait for, while it begins its turn at once, so a resumed subagent can run with no page: the stop has taken the page away and the put-up has not landed. With no page every change call is refused through `noPageSaid`. Three causes sit behind that one refusal and cannot be told apart: the put-up is still queued, the put-up refused, or no put-up was ever fired. The first two clear on a start event rather than on elapsed time, each SubagentStart firing a fresh put-up; whether waiting inside one turn clears them is unknown. `landingAgain` retries only where the reason names the lock or a put-back, so a landing refused for anything else is retried by nothing. A take-down also drops the reading record, so the agent owes its required reading again.

evidence:
One case, timed. Seat `nimue` resumed subagent `a62ddc0cb2ee9da93` at 16:11:11.533Z; its first turn lands 2.1 seconds later. Its page had gone at 16:10:31Z under the take-down for the previous return, `c0d2c598e27`, and the put-up for the resume landed only at 16:12:41Z, `414363d4fc9` — 89.5 seconds after the resume. In that interval the subagent made its only two change calls, drafting a `change-file` edit at 16:12:24.196Z and asking to list what it had kept at 16:12:31.777Z. Both were refused. It tried no more, and ended its turn at 16:13:29.432Z saying it was going to stop rather than work around it. The page it wanted had been there since 16:12:41Z: ten seconds after its last attempt, forty-eight seconds before it gave up.

What moves a page, and on what signal. `agent/hook/agent-hook/state-subagent/state-subagent.agent-hook.code.ts:113-115` calls `puttingUp` at a SubagentStart payload and `takingDown` at a SubagentStop, and the hook registers at those two events only. Each spawns a detached process running `agent/subagent/modules/presence/subagent-presence.module.code.ts` and is not waited on, the hook being given five seconds. The take-down is `took` at `:190-210`, landing `change-mechanical-file/remove-file-page` under `<slug> is done, so its page goes; what it was is in this repository's history` at `:208-209`. Nothing on that path reads how old a page is or looks for a live process.

What a resume restores, and how late. `wrote` at `:111-156` rebuilds a returning subagent's page out of `subagentPageInHistory`, minted id and all, and lands `<slug>: a subagent resuming takes up the page it had` at `:151-152`. A resume does restore the page. It restores it through `runMechanicalChange`, which takes `.git/akasha-landing.lock` and waits up to the 300 seconds `WAITED_AT_MOST` states, and `landingAgain` at `agent/subagent/modules/landing-again/subagent-landing-again.module.code.ts:33-43` retries five times at 30-second waits where the reason names that lock or a put-back. Nothing refused in the window above: the 89.5 seconds went on waiting for the lock behind other landings.

The census is a second reaper, it did not do this, and it cannot mend it. The subagent sweep judges each page WORKING, STALE or UNDETERMINED at `agent/subagent/modules/census/subagent-census.module.code.ts:143`; only STALE goes, and nothing schedules it. `pagesIn` enumerates pages from the index, so an agent with no page is not in the census at all.

What the agent reads. The first clause is `command/modules/change-acting/change-acting.module.code.ts:24` exactly: `this call names no agent whose page the edits would be kept beside`. `noPageSaid` at line 59 adds `PAGE_LANDING` from line 26. Draft, list, apply, show and drop all answer through it, so a page-less agent cannot even list what it kept. The page is found by `agentPathOf` at `domain/context/modules/warranting/warranting.module.code.ts:365-367`, out of the index and nowhere else.

The third cause, measured on this page's own writer. `nimue-a6f6ed863db6cd5fe` was taken down at 10:32:48 on a correct stop and resumed. Eight minutes later no put-up commit existed and the seat's log held zero occurrences of its id, while put-ups for other subagents landed that minute: the lock was free and the machinery working. No SubagentStart fired at all, and that variant never clears by waiting.

Cause two clears, and not on a clock. `state-subagent.agent-hook.code.ts:113-115` fires `puttingUp` at every SubagentStart, so each new turn asks for a fresh put-up whatever the last one did. A put-up refused is therefore not terminal — but what clears it is the next start event, not elapsed time. Whether an agent retrying inside one turn ever sees it clear is not established here.

A second case, and the scale behind it. `athena-ac3f05d42421ae25f` landed `8778562` at 09:58:19 -0600 on 2026-09-13 and was reaped 137 seconds later at 10:00:36, `4b58611a0da`. Its put-up that second refused rather than queuing: `subagent-presence.log:43`, 10:00:36.431, `holds a body already, so nothing is added` — the add-file answer at `change/modules/answer/change-answer.module.code.ts:161`, a reason `worthAnotherTry` does not retry. The page came back at 10:06:10, `88a2580e06b`, 334 seconds page-less, and was reaped again at 10:08:56. The agent reported four refusals over roughly seven minutes and a fifth call that worked. Across 2026-09-13, 82 reap commits landed and 19, 23.2%, were followed by a restore for the same id: mean gap 163 seconds, longest 679 (`ember-a9ba157c93365e2fa`, reaped and restored nine times that day). 23.2% is a floor rather than a rate — a subagent reaped mid-work that never resumed leaves no restore commit, so nothing here counts it.

What is not verified. Neither case was reproduced; both rest on an agent's report plus the commits, the presence log line and the code path. The interleaving behind `holds a body already` is undetermined: `wrote:122` must have found the path absent while the answer step moments later found it held, and what re-materialised it in that window is not established. What is established is the weaker claim this rests on — nothing orders the take-down against the put-up, and both decide against an unlocked read of the working tree before `applied` takes the lock.

What would close the gap rather than soften it: stop taking the page down at SubagentStop and let the census reap instead. At a resume the page would still be there and `wrote` returns early, so no landing runs. It needs a service to schedule it, which nothing does.
